rows.speaker: أبو سفيان
rows.claim: Abu Sufyan reports Heraclius's questions about Muhammad's lineage, reputation, ancestry, followers, apostasy, honesty, wars, and message; Heraclius reads the answers as prophetic signs and predicts Muhammad will rule.
rows.anchor: أَنَّ عَبْدَ اللَّهِ بْنَ عَبَّاسٍ، أَخْبَرَهُ أَنَّ أَبَا سُفْيَانَ بْنَ حَرْبٍ أَخْبَرَهُ أَنَّ هِرَقْلَ أَرْسَلَ إِلَيْهِ

rows.speaker: محمد
rows.claim: Muhammad's letter to Heraclius invites him to Islam and quotes 3:64 as a call to worship Allah alone, renounce shirk and human lordship, and affirm Muslims' identity if the addressees turn away.
rows.anchor: مِنْ مُحَمَّدٍ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ إِلَى هِرَقْلَ عَظِيمِ الرُّومِ

rows.speaker: أبو سفيان
rows.claim: After the letter is read, Roman notables protest and Abu Sufyan concludes Heraclius fears Muhammad; Abu Sufyan remained convinced Muhammad would prevail until he himself entered Islam.
rows.anchor: قَالَ أَبُو سُفْيَانَ فَلَمَّا قَالَ مَا قَالَ، وَفَرَغَ مِنْ قِرَاءَةِ الْكِتَابِ كَثُرَ عِنْدَهُ الصَّخَبُ

rows.speaker: ابن الناظور
rows.claim: Ibn al-Natur reports that Heraclius read the stars as foretelling a circumcised king, confirmed the messenger and Arabs were circumcised, received a learned Roman's agreement that a prophet had appeared, then failed to secure Roman allegiance and recast his appeal as a test.
rows.anchor: وَكَانَ ابْنُ النَّاظُورِ صَاحِبُ إِيلِيَاءَ وَهِرَقْلَ سُقُفًّا عَلَى نَصَارَى الشَّأْمِ، يُحَدِّثُ

rows.speaker: أبو سفيان
rows.claim: Abu Sufyan recounts Heraclius's questions about Muhammad's reputation, ancestry, following, apostasy, fidelity, battles, and orders; Heraclius reads the answers as prophetic signs and predicts Muhammad's rule.
rows.anchor: قَالَ أَبُو سُفْيَانَ وَاللَّهِ لَوْلاَ الْحَيَاءُ يَوْمَئِذٍ مِنْ أَنْ يَأْثُرَ أَصْحَابِي عَنِّي الْكَذِبَ

rows.speaker: محمد
rows.claim: The Prophet's letter to Caesar urges conversion to Islam, promises a double reward, warns of the subjects' sin if he refuses, and quotes 3:64's call to shared monotheism.
rows.anchor: مِنْ مُحَمَّدٍ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ، إِلَى هِرَقْلَ عَظِيمِ الرُّومِ، سَلَامٌ عَلَى مَنِ اتَّبَعَ الْهُدَى

rows.speaker: أبو سفيان
rows.claim: After Heraclius reads the letter, Roman dignitaries protest; Abu Sufyan says the king fears Muhammad and he remained certain Muhammad's cause would prevail until entering Islam, though unwillingly.
rows.anchor: قَالَ أَبُو سُفْيَانَ وَاللَّهِ مَا زِلْتُ ذَلِيلًا مُسْتَيْقِنًا بِأَنَّ أَمْرَهُ سَيَظْهَرُ، حَتَّى أَدْخَلَ اللَّهُ قَلْبِي الْإِسْلَامَ وَأَنَا كَارِهٌ
